evals.prompt: Turn the bundled synthetic inventory files into a local working app. I need stock search, a low-stock view, editable reorder levels/notes and CSV export. Launch it, edit SKU 00128's reorder level to 20, import the next products snapshot and show how I choose between local20 and source14. Verify export and persistence.
evals.expected_output: Running app and source; exact SKU retained; source stock updates to9; local20 survives pending conflict; local/source decision works; export contains chosen value; state survives restart.
assertions: Outputs a running operational app, not only a plan

evals.prompt: Build me a local contact follow-up app from contacts.csv and activities.csv. I need to search contacts, edit status and next_action, view activities and export contacts. Keep contact IDs exactly as written. When I import the next contacts snapshot, my local corrections should survive; show conflicting source changes for a choice and retain missing contacts for review. Launch the app and verify a second import. Use synthetic local data only.
evals.expected_output: Usable contact app with independently keyed activities, local status/next_action editing and snapshot import/conflict workflow; executed main actions on the held-out contacts domain.
assertions: Uses contact_id and activity_id without lossy coercion
Contact0001 local status survives unchanged source
Unedited company changes to North Studio Europe
Does not multiply contacts because one has two activities

evals.prompt: Make a recurring-import client tracker from a CSV with only name, company and status. Two rows share the same name/company and none of these fields is stable. I need to edit status and import next month safely. What do you do before building the import behavior?
evals.expected_output: Identifies missing durable identity and requests one material business decision or stable ID; does not silently deduplicate distinct clients, invent identity or claim safe future reconciliation.
assertions: Recognizes statistical uniqueness is not stable identity
Does not merge distinct duplicate-looking clients
Asks a focused material identity question or scopes a read-only alternative
